gaps.note: All 21 networks. The owner set the cycle 8 focus on opcodes and their client implementations on 2026-11-24, but the plan (cycles/008/plan.json) dates from 2026-11-23 and its two network units ran the older angles: ethereum-reference and established-l1 spent their findings on tokens (ten sender-charged tokens, the yUSD/yETH/xSolvBTC blocks, sNVB) and on gas caps, and neither file runs tools/opdiff or reads an interpreter. The other 17 networks had no network unit this cycle. The two code units are the only opcode-focused work, and both test the deployed bytecode only. The opcode question for cycle 9 therefore stands exactly where OPCODES.md left it, including its own list of what is not covered.

Monad. The opcode battery, pmdiff and pmdiff2 all go through eth_call, and eth_call always runs the interpreter (OPCODES.md check 4), so the 185,529 vectors say nothing about the x86 code that blocks run for the PoolManager. Only the 2,176 mined swaps reach the compiled path. Critic reading on 2026-11-24 of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp: jumpi_comparison (lines 3677-3731) tests all four limbs of a non-deferred condition (vptest of the whole ymm register, or an OR of the four 64 bit words), and shift_by_literal (5078-5107) plus shift_avx_reg_by_literal (4990-5076) give zero for SHL/SHR by 256 or more, sign fill for SAR, and a correct lane permutation and carry for every dword and bit shift as read. Not read: the deferred comparison paths (LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO folded into the JUMPI), SDIV, SMOD, MULMOD, ADDMOD and SIGNEXTEND with non-literal operands, and the new shift_literal_by_non_literal of v0.16.6 (see the first high lead). Current facts page: mainnet and testnet both on v0.16.5 with MONAD_TEN (https://docs.monad.xyz/ai/current-facts.md).

Monad. MONAD_TEN (MIP-8, page-encoded storage) has been canonical on mainnet since 2026-09-02 14:30 UTC (https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/upgrade-instructions/page-storage-mip-8-migration and the v0.16.1 release notes). The storage layer now addresses every slot as page_index = slot >> 7 and offset = slot & 0x7F (https://mips.monad.xyz/MIPs/MIP-8). Earlier cycles judged MIP-8 for gas only (state/cleared.json, cycle 1 high-throughput, A9). The cycle 8 bits unit tested slot folding with the 256 single-bit indexes through extsload, which cannot catch a fault in a multi-bit mapping such as a truncated page index or a wrong offset recombination, and its own lead on this is marked low. The mined swap replay covers only slots that real pools touch.

Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium. Check 4 of OPCODES.md read only interpreters that are not go-ethereum or stock revm, and the Nitro go-ethereum fork was left out on the grounds that it is go-ethereum. Earlier cycles read only core/vm/eips.go and evm.go of OffchainLabs/go-ethereum (f3a966e, 0e44603), not instructions.go, interpreter.go, jump_table.go or the jump destination analysis. Critic query on 2026-11-24: https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc answers web3_clientVersion with nitro/v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f-20261116T155937Z/linux-arm64/go1.27.3, so at least one public node runs an arm64 build made with Go 1.27.3, and holiman/uint256 compiles to different math/bits intrinsics on arm64. Which architecture answered the battery and which the sequencer runs is not recorded. Elysium still reports nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown (linux-amd64, go1.25.12).

Celo. Critic queries on 2026-11-24: three calls of web3_clientVersion on https://forno.celo.org returned reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb twice and Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 (go1.24.13) once. The battery, pmdiff and the mined swap check do not record which of the two answered each request, so the Celo row of OPCODES.md may rest on either client or a mix. The Geth build is in neither the check 4 table nor the ruint table, and which client produces blocks is still open (L-245, L-262).

Polygon. The RPC in state/networks.json, https://polygon.drpc.org, answered web3_clientVersion with Geth/v10.0.0/drpc on 2026-11-24, which is an aggregator label, not a client. The Polygon results of the battery and of pmdiff may have been served by bor or by another client behind drpc. established-l1 used https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com for its own calls.

BNB Smart Chain. reth-bsc is missing from the ruint table of OPCODES.md although a public endpoint runs it (established-l1 profile L2). Critic read on 2026-11-24 of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix/Cargo.lock: ruint 1.18.0, revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1, the same on v0.1.4 and main. So it never ran the withdrawn ruint 1.21.0. This closes that one row. reth-bsc's own interpreter changes, if any, were not read.

HyperEVM and Avalanche. The mined swap check is the only test that reaches the HyperEVM validator, which is closed source, and it rests on 14 swaps (5 paired). For Avalanche it rests on 59 swaps (29 paired), and the verifier of established-l1 asks whether the saevm path read this cycle is the one live on mainnet. No unit extended the log window.

Unichain. pmdiff and pmdiff2 place the Ethereum PoolManager runtime at a fresh address on every network, so the 550 scripts never ran Unichain's own genesis predeploy (24,050 bytes). The 6,019 mined swaps are the only behaviour evidence for that bytecode. Leads L-092 and L-426 are still open.

All 21 networks. Still no build of this checkout. The cycle 8 settlement unit filed its rollback probe again as a lead that waits for solc 0.8.26 (see duplicates). Every opcode result therefore holds for the deployed bytecode and for a Python transcription of src/, not for the build that will be deployed.

Tempo. The jump destination scan of evm2 picks vector code by CPU at run time, and only the endpoint's CPU was tested (OPCODES.md). Whether validators build with the optional jit feature (L-286) decides whether Tempo has the same untested compiled path as Monad. No cycle 8 unit held Tempo.

Either the charge only on transfers to a listed pair, which any caller can name as take recipient, is the distinguishing fact that keeps F-092 unprivileged, or F-092 should be re-rated pool-creator.

leads.question: Monad v0.16.6 (released 2026-11-18, not yet on mainnet, which runs v0.16.5) adds Emitter::shift_literal_by_non_literal (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.6/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp, from about line 5253, called from shift_by_non_literal near line 5231). It shifts a literal value by a variable amount through two unaligned loads from a 96 byte rodata window. Transcribe that routine (rodata_.add96 layout, window and bit_mask offsets, destructive_mov_stack_elem_to_bounded_rax with bound 256) into Python and compare it with SHL, SHR and SAR for every shift 0 to 256 and for the literal values src/ uses this way: 1 at TickBitmap.sol:73 and :110, 2^256-1 at TickBitmap.sol:97, 0x8421084210842108cc6318c6db6d54be at BitMath.sol:22, plus negative values for SAR. Also state which v0.16.5 path handled these shifts before (its shift_by_non_literal returns early for a literal value only when that value is 0, or all ones under SAR, at emitter.cpp lines 5117-5127).
leads.why: These shifts build the bit masks of TickBitmap.flipTick and nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord and the lookup table of mostSignificantBit. A wrong mask on the compiled path, which eth_call never runs, would make swaps skip or invent initialized ticks in every Monad pool once validators adopt the release. Tick and liquidity accounting would then diverge from the positions, which other users could exploit.

leads.question: In the v0.16.5 x86 emitter of Monad, which instructions does the compiler emit inline and which does it hand to the runtime's shared uint256 library: LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ and ISZERO as deferred comparisons fused into JUMPI, and SDIV, SMOD, MULMOD, ADDMOD, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE with non-literal operands? For each inline path, check by reading or transcription the edges in the OPCODES.md table: SLT and SGT across the sign bit, SDIV of -2^255 by -1, SMOD sign, SIGNEXTEND index 2 and 15 and above 31, BYTE index above 31.
leads.why: The PoolManager is compiled on Monad because it is called often, and no battery vector reaches compiled code. Signed comparisons and SDIV/SMOD decide tick rounding in TickBitmap.compress (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:38 and nearby) and the swap direction checks in Pool.swap. An inline fault on attacker-chosen ticks or amounts would compute other prices or deltas only in blocks.

leads.question: Under MIP-8 (live since 2026-09-02), can two distinct storage slots of one contract resolve to the same (page_index, offset) or read back each other's values? Test with eth_call and state overrides on https://rpc.monad.xyz: a probe contract writes slots s and reads s XOR k for k over all masks in bits 0 to 7, over bit 7 to 8 boundaries, and for page indexes near 2^249 - 1. Also compare eth_getStorageAt with PoolManager.extsload for the four tick info slots and three position slots of live pools whose keccak base lies within 4 of a 128 boundary, so that one record spans two pages.
leads.why: Every pool mapping, tick record and ERC-6909 balance is a keccak slot plus a small offset. A page-layer fault that merged or misplaced slots would let a caller-chosen tick, salt or currency id overwrite another user's position or claim. The single-bit test of cycle 8 cannot see a multi-bit fault.

leads.question: At the go-ethereum submodule commit pinned by nitro v3.12.4 (0e44603), and at b72783f once it is public, do core/vm/instructions.go, interpreter.go, jump_table.go and analysis_legacy.go (or the jump destination code that commit uses) change any opcode in the OPCODES.md table, the jump destination set, RETURNDATACOPY bounds or the ordering of the CALL success flag, compared with what the EVM specification requires? Read them against the spec, not against upstream.

leads.question: Call web3_clientVersion before and after each battery chunk on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc and the Robinhood endpoint, and rerun the targeted MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV and shift vectors (tools/opdiff/targeted.py 42161 4663) until both linux-arm64 and linux-amd64 builds have answered, if both exist. Does the Go 1.27 issue tracker list a miscompile of math/bits Mul64, Add64, Sub64 or Div64, or of shifts, on arm64 that is fixed after go1.27.3? A sequencer-only arithmetic fault would put wrong pool math into blocks before any challenge.

leads.question: In evm2 at the revision Tempo v1.19.0 pins, list every CPU-specific branch of the jump destination scan (AVX2, AVX-512, SSE, NEON, scalar). Transcribe each into Python and run them on the 24,009 byte PoolManager runtime and on adversarial bytecode with PUSH32 data that contains 0x5b at every lane position. Do all branches give the same jump destination set? Does any validator build use the jit feature (L-286)?
leads.why: A validator that accepts a jump into push data, or rejects a valid JUMPDEST, would compute other results for the same transaction. With one client, that becomes a fork or a wrong canonical state.

leads.question: Did ruint publish a release after 1.21.1 that fixes another fault in the paths 1.21.0 rewrote (div, mul, shifts, add_mod, the 2^256 - 1 fast path)? Read the changelog and the diff of each release after 1.21.1, and the ruint pin of reth main and tempo main. If a later fix exists, run its trigger condition through tools/opdiff/targeted.py on chain ids 1 and 4217.
leads.why: Tempo runs the rewritten paths on a single client, and mulDiv in FullMath takes the 2^256 - 1 MULMOD on every call.
